system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

answer.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding/signup friction as the lever with the most direct causal link to both: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifted first-week activation). Activation messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable second choice but treats the symptom further downstream; friction reduction plausibly feeds it. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 says it does acquire price-sensitive SMBs but materially damaged 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it. Competitive pressure is exactly the situation that tempts over-generalization of that result, and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not this quarter's logo count. Referral incentive (memory_57) works on established customers and does nothing for the two declining funnel metrics. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is real but is a different segment from where the bleeding is.

I spend both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two memories my chosen action rests on entirely, and both are consolidated summaries whose original records I have not seen. Key things I want from the archive: (a) was the effect measured on completion/activation only, or did it carry through to retained, qualified revenue; (b) which segments and which fields were actually cut; (c) effect size and whether it was durable past week one. I do not need to verify memory_73 to act, since I am declining the action it warns about — verifying it could only tempt me to relitigate a caveat that is already directionally clear.

Downstream value risk flagged: cutting signup fields and onboarding steps removes qualification and firmographic data, which is precisely the input the sales-assisted enterprise path (memory_44) depends on. An over-simplified top of funnel can raise activation while lowering pipeline quality — a metric-up, revenue-down failure. So this runs as a standard experiment with self-serve/SMB scoping, an untouched enterprise demo-request path, and guardrails on 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline mix, not just completion and activation. Uncertainty preserved: these lifts were measured on an earlier funnel under different competitive conditions; a 4-6% QoQ decline may be partly competitor-driven mix shift rather than friction, in which case friction reduction underperforms its inherited effect size. If verification shows memory_86 or memory_31 measured only week-one proxies with no revenue follow-through, I would narrow to a small_guarded_test and add activation_messaging as the fallback for the next slot.
